subject: Private DNS stitching & termination responsibilities for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-payments.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@acme-payments.com, security@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private DNS stitching and TLS termination – quick sync

Vanessa / Neha,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We sketched a couple of options for how Acme will expose private endpoints to the Redwood Private runtime inside our VPC:

Option A: Delegate acme.internal -> Redwood resolver via a stub zone + Redwood terminator (edge inside our account).
Option B: Keep acme.internal authoritative in our DNS, and have Redwood terminate TLS at an internal proxy we host (proxy presents customer cert).

Security wants clarity on who holds the leaf certs, who rotates them, and whether OCSP/CRL checks will cross accounts. Attached is a quick diagram and our list of certificate authorities.

Ask: can you confirm which option Redwood prefers operationally, and an owner matrix for CSR generation + rotation?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Payments
attachments: dns-stitching-diagram-v1.png, private-csr-inventory.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-payments.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private DNS stitching and TLS termination – quick sync

Jordan — thanks for the clear options and diagram. High level: Redwood can support both patterns but we recommend a single, unambiguous termination point to simplify audit and tracing. My recommended approach (hybrid):

- Use a stub zone for acme.internal pointed at a private resolver we run in your VPC (so we can resolve private service names without authoritative delegation).
- Terminate TLS at a customer-controlled internal proxy (Option B) for any traffic requiring customer-managed keys (regulated workloads).
- For non-regulated traffic, Redwood-managed terminator inside a dedicated subnet in your VPC (Option A) gives lower ops overhead.

Owner matrix (proposal):
- CSR generation: Customer (Acme) for regulated leaf certs / Redwood for Redwood-managed leaf certs.
- Root/Intermediates: Customer-managed (Acme) if you require control; otherwise Redwood-provided intermediate pinned to our audit trail.
- Rotation windows: 90 days for customer-managed (we accept ACME/automated), 60 days for Redwood-managed by default.
- OCSP/CRL: OCSP stapling by terminator; Redwood can staple for Redwood-managed certs; for customer-managed certs we require OCSP responder access or acceptable CRL distribution.

Action items for both sides:
1) Acme: confirm which hostnames must be customer-managed vs Redwood-managed.
2) Redwood (Neha/Jonas): produce playbook for stub zone creation, resolver ACL, and terminator placement.
3) Security (Rishi): quick risk assessment for OCSP responder access across VPC boundary.

I'll loop in a short playbook draft tomorrow.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-payments.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private DNS stitching and TLS termination – playbook first pass

Jordan / team — attaching a first-pass playbook below (inline). See also the diagram Jordan shared.

Playbook (first pass):
1) DNS stitching
   - Customer (Acme) creates a stub zone acme.internal -> pointing to Redwood's resolver endpoints (IP list provided).
   - Redwood provides resolver endpoints inside your VPC subnets (private IPs) with a security-group whitelist.
   - Transactional TTLs: 30s for endpoints we expect frequent change; 300s for stable service records.

2) Terminator placement decision matrix
   - Customer-managed terminator (recommended for regulated hostnames): benefits = customer key custody, no cross-account KMS access; cons = customer ops overhead.
   - Redwood-managed terminator (recommended for scale/non-regulated): benefits = automated rotation, stapling, integrated tracing; cons = customer must accept Redwood intermediate or provide cross-account trust.

3) Certificate lifecycle & rotation
   - If customer-managed: Acme creates and rotates leaf certs; Redwood validates via CSR proof (signed challenge). We store only the public chain; private keys never leave Acme.
   - If Redwood-managed: Redwood will request CSRs from internal CA/automated ACME endpoint; we provide rotation logs and audit proof.

4) OCSP/CRL and stapling
   - Redwood will staple OCSP for Redwood-managed certs. For customer-managed certs, we require either: (a) stapled OCSP responses uploaded to a secure S3 accessible to Redwood terminators, or (b) an OCSP responder endpoint reachable from terminator subnets.

5) Testing & rollback
   - Canary hostnames in a non-prod zone first.
   - Fallback: resolver re-point to authoritative Acme NS on failure.

Please confirm the stub-zone IPs and whether Acme can host an OCSP responder or prefers file-based stapling. Also propose a maintenance window for CSR handoff (we usually prefer low-traffic late-night windows).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Platform SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: private-csr-inventory.csv

From: Jordan Mills <jordan@acme-payments.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private DNS stitching and TLS termination – playbook first pass

Neha / Vanessa — this is great, thanks. We will: 
- Confirm the list of regulated hostnames by EOD Monday.
- Stand up an OCSP responder reachable from the private subnet (infra@ will follow up with IP allowlist and cert for the responder).
- We prefer customer-managed keys for payment-facing hostnames and Redwood-managed for analytics/internal-facing endpoints.

One clarification: for the stub zone approach, will Redwood's resolver perform recursion for external lookups, or will it forward to our existing resolvers? We need to ensure split-horizon behavior doesn't leak internal records.

Agreed on maintenance windows — propose Sunday 0200–0400 PT.

Jordan
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Payments
